exposure: Brief D5.md required reading docs/ paths, but this seat's focus (method step 4: code comments) touched no docs/*.md content and read no earlier audit record. In-code comments across custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py routinely cite issue numbers (#NNN) and prior-round finding ids (e.g. R1-D0-02, R5-D1-06, R6-D0-02) as historical context inside their own explanations -- these were read as part of sampling every >3-line comment (COMMON.md/D5.md's method), never used to select or motivate a finding, and none of the two findings below rest on anything those citations said. RELEASE_NOTES.md is present in this export (COMMON.md keeps it for tests/entities.py) but was not used to check any docs claim -- that is s1's structure/content scope, not this seat's (code comments only).

findings.title: Two >3-line code comments name a symbol as a bare shorthand that has zero code occurrence, beside the real full name
findings.claim: In custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/const.py:80 and optimizer.py:6519, a >3-line comment abbreviates a real, checkable production symbol (CONF_HEAT_PUMP_MIN_POWER; min_electrical_power) down to a bare form (MIN_POWER; min_power) that occurs nowhere in the tree's actual code, in the same comment block that correctly names or uses the symbol's real form.
findings.mechanism: const.py:80 reads "``CONF_HEAT_PUMP_MAX_POWER`` / ``MIN_POWER`` are nameplate limits" -- the sibling constant is CONF_HEAT_PUMP_MIN_POWER (const.py:656); grep -rnw MIN_POWER over custom_components/+tests/ (*.py,*.mjs), excluding comment-only lines, returns nothing. optimizer.py:6515-6519 reads "No lower clamp to ``min_electrical_power`` ... Forcing the baseline up to the minimum modulation power made it burn a constant min_power * 24 h per day" -- the same block backtick-names the real attribute self.model.params.min_electrical_power (used at optimizer.py:2131, :3719, :3751, :5809, :6766, :6814 etc.) two sentences earlier, then drops to the bare, non-existent min_power in the very next sentence describing the same quantity.

findings.metric_definition: shorthand_missing = count of tokens in a >3-line comment/docstring with 0 code occurrences whose words are a proper subset of a real identifier's in the same file.
findings.phenomenon_property: a >3-line code comment names, by a bare (non-backticked-resolving) abbreviation, a production symbol it also names correctly (or a strict superset name of it) elsewhere in the same block or file, and the abbreviation itself is not a valid reference to anything in the tree
findings.seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round8/D5/s2_comment_idents.py (the SHORTHAND lines in its stdout enumerate every seam)
reproduction_steps: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1 VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 python3 tools/audit/round8/D5/s2_comment_idents.py
confirm the two SHORTHAND lines and RESULT shorthand_missing=2
apply the two one-line comment edits described in perturbation.change
re-run the same command; confirm RESULT shorthand_missing=0
revert the two edits; confirm `diff -rq custom_components/heatpump_optimizer <baseline>/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer` is empty
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Two one-line comment edits (const.py:80, optimizer.py:6518), no behavioural change; a fixer should also grep-check any other bare occurrence of these two specific abbreviations before closing, since this finding's harness is scoped to >3-line blocks and does not scan single-line comments.

non_findings.claim: Every backtick/double-backtick-quoted identifier cited in a module docstring or >3-line comment under custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py resolves to a real, checkable symbol somewhere in the tree once dunder methods (Python protocol names, not project symbols), commit-hash citations, and named-external-repository symbols (a different project's file/function, explicitly attributed by repo+SHA in the same sentence) are excluded.
non_findings.value: RESULT backtick_missing=7 raw, of which 2 are dunder/hash noise (__float__, fda9bed), 2 name a different repository's own code on purpose (fault_description, and the earlier device_config/device_name_slug pair filtered by the same rule), 2 are the exact pair already reported as D5-s2-01 (MIN_POWER counted again here since it happens to also be backticked; min_power in optimizer.py is NOT backticked so does not appear in this list), and 1 (MixedHotWater at thermal_model.py:1830) is an explicitly-labelled 'convention' name paired one clause later with the real coordinator._dhw_mixed_water, not a bare symbol claim -- judged not a finding.
